name: L293D dual H-bridge motor driver
description: Texas Instruments L293D quadruple half-H driver with built-in output clamp diodes: drivers 1-2 (enable 1,2EN) and 3-4 (enable 3,4EN) form two H-bridges, so it runs two small DC motors forwards, backwards, braked or coasting (or one bipolar stepper), 600 mA per channel (1.2 A peak), motor supply VCC2 4.5-36 V, logic supply VCC1 4.5-7 V, TTL inputs that accept 3.3 V GPIOs. buildNotes: Truth table (TI function table): EN high + 1A high/2A low = forward, 1A low/2A high = reverse, 1A = 2A = fast brake; EN low = outputs off, motor coasts.
VCC1 (pin 16) is the logic supply and needs 4.5-7 V: wire it to 5 V, not 3.3 V. The A and EN inputs still accept 3.3 V GPIO highs (>= 2.3 V).
VCC2 (pin 8) is the motor supply, from VCC1 up to 36 V. Use a separate battery for anything bigger than a tiny motor, and join its minus to GND.
Connect all four GND pins (4, 5, 12, 13) to ground: they are also the heat sink. Share ground with the microcontroller.
Each channel is limited to 600 mA continuous (1.2 A for 100 us). Motor stall current often exceeds this; the chip shuts down when it overheats.
The outputs drop about 2.6 V typical (3.6 V max) across the bridge at 600 mA, so budget extra supply voltage.
Put 100 nF ceramic capacitors from VCC1 and VCC2 to GND close to the chip, plus a bulk electrolytic on VCC2.
Tie an unused enable (3,4EN) to GND rather than leaving it floating.

driver.code:
# L293D quadruple half-H driver (TI L293D / ST L293D), MicroPython driver for ONE H-bridge (one DC motor).
# Two half-H drivers that share an enable form one bridge:
#   bridge 1: inputs 1A (pin 2) and 2A (pin 7), enable 1,2EN (pin 1), motor on 1Y (pin 3) / 2Y (pin 6)
#   bridge 2: inputs 3A (pin 10) and 4A (pin 15), enable 3,4EN (pin 9), motor on 3Y (pin 11) / 4Y (pin 14)
# Function table (TI SLRS008D, Table 1, each driver): EN = H, A = H -> Y = H; EN = H, A = L -> Y = L;
# EN = L -> Y = Z (high impedance). So for one bridge:
#   EN = H, A1 = H, A2 = L  -> forward
#   EN = H, A1 = L, A2 = H  -> reverse
#   EN = H, A1 = A2         -> fast motor stop (brake: both motor leads at the same level)
#   EN = L                  -> outputs off, the motor coasts to a stop
# Inputs are TTL compatible: low <= 1.5 V, high >= 2.3 V, so 3.3 V GPIOs drive them directly.
# Speed: PWM the enable pin (a few kHz or less; the outputs switch in about 1 us).
from machine import Pin, PWM


class L293D:
    def __init__(self, in_a, in_b, en=None, freq=1000):
        """in_a, in_b: GPIO numbers wired to the bridge's A inputs (1A/2A or 3A/4A).
        en: GPIO number wired to 1,2EN or 3,4EN, or None when that enable pin is tied to 5 V (always on)."""
        self.a = Pin(in_a, Pin.OUT, value=0)
        self.b = Pin(in_b, Pin.OUT, value=0)
        self.pwm = None
        if en is not None:
            self.pwm = PWM(Pin(en), freq=freq, duty_u16=0)

    def _enable(self, speed):
        if self.pwm is not None:
            speed = max(0, min(100, speed))
            self.pwm.duty_u16(speed * 65535 // 100)

    def forward(self, speed=100):
        """Spin one way (A1 high, A2 low). speed 0-100 % needs the enable pin on a GPIO."""
        self.a.value(1)
        self.b.value(0)
        self._enable(speed)

    def reverse(self, speed=100):
        """Spin the other way (A1 low, A2 high)."""
        self.a.value(0)
        self.b.value(1)
        self._enable(speed)

    def brake(self):
        """Fast motor stop: both inputs low with the drivers enabled (both motor leads pulled to GND)."""
        self.a.value(0)
        self.b.value(0)
        self._enable(100)

    def coast(self):
        """Free-running stop: enable low, outputs high impedance. Without an enable GPIO this falls back to brake()."""
        self.a.value(0)
        self.b.value(0)
        if self.pwm is not None:
            self.pwm.duty_u16(0)

    def stop(self):
        self.coast()

example.code:
import time
from l293d import L293D

# Motor 1 between 1Y and 2Y; 1,2EN on a PWM pin.
motor = L293D({1A}, {2A}, en={1_2EN})
while True:
    motor.forward()
    print('motor 1 forward')
    time.sleep(1)
    motor.coast()
    print('motor 1 off')
    time.sleep(1)

name: part-l293d
description: Pinout, electrical limits, wiring and MicroPython driver for the L293D dual H-bridge motor driver chip (TI L293DNE, quadruple half-H driver, DIP-16). Use when designing, wiring, simulating or writing code for an L293D in a Sparkbench project or any ESP32 / Raspberry Pi Pico / Raspberry Pi build.

# L293D dual H-bridge motor driver (L293DNE)

## Overview
The **L293D** is four half-H drivers in one chip. Drivers 1 and 2 share the enable 1,2EN and drivers 3 and 4 share 3,4EN, so each pair is a full H-bridge: two small DC motors forwards/backwards (or one bipolar stepper), up to **600 mA per channel** (1.2 A peak for 100 us) at 4.5-36 V. The "D" version has the output clamp diodes built in, so no external flyback diodes are needed. Inputs are TTL, so 3.3 V GPIOs drive it directly. Hobbyists buy the bare **Texas Instruments L293DNE in a DIP-16 package** (ST's L293D has the same pinout) and plug it straight into a breadboard.

## Pinout (DIP-16, pin 1 next to the notch)
| Pin | Name | Function |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | 1,2EN | Enable drivers 1 and 2 (bridge 1), active high; PWM for speed |
| 2 | 1A | Driver 1 input |
| 3 | 1Y | Driver 1 output (motor 1 lead) |
| 4, 5 | GND | Ground and heat sink |
| 6 | 2Y | Driver 2 output (motor 1 other lead) |
| 7 | 2A | Driver 2 input |
| 8 | VCC2 | Motor supply, VCC1 to 36 V |
| 9 | 3,4EN | Enable drivers 3 and 4 (bridge 2), active high |
| 10 | 3A | Driver 3 input |
| 11 | 3Y | Driver 3 output (motor 2 lead) |
| 12, 13 | GND | Ground and heat sink |
| 14 | 4Y | Driver 4 output (motor 2 other lead) |
| 15 | 4A | Driver 4 input |
| 16 | VCC1 | Logic supply, 4.5-7 V (5 V) |

## Electrical limits
- VCC1 (logic): 4.5-7 V recommended (5 V). It is NOT a 3.3 V part: never run VCC1 from 3V3.
- VCC2 (motor): from VCC1 up to 36 V (absolute max 36 V).
- Inputs: high >= 2.3 V, low <= 1.5 V, absolute max 7 V.
- Output current: **600 mA continuous per channel**, 1.2 A peak (non-repetitive, <= 100 us).
- Voltage drop: high side up to 1.8 V, low side up to 1.8 V at 600 mA, so a motor sees about VCC2 - 2.6 V (typ) to VCC2 - 3.6 V (max).
- Logic supply current up to 60 mA, motor supply idle current up to 24 mA. Operating range 0-70 C.

## Interface details (datasheet function table, each driver)
| A | EN | Y |
|---|---|---|
| H | H | H |
| L | H | L |
| X | L | Z (off) |

For one bridge (motor between 1Y and 2Y):
| 1,2EN | 1A | 2A | Motor |
|---|---|---|---|
| H | H | L | Forward |
| H | L | H | Reverse |
| H | 1A = 2A | | Fast stop (brake) |
| L | X | X | Coasts to a stop |
Bridge 2 is the same with 3,4EN, 3A, 4A. In thermal shutdown all outputs go off.

## Wiring
- Power: VCC1 (pin 16) -> 5 V (ESP32 5V/VIN, Pico VBUS). VCC2 (pin 8) -> motor battery + (or 5 V for a tiny motor). All four GND pins (4, 5, 12, 13) -> GND, shared with the battery minus and the microcontroller GND.
- ESP32: 1,2EN -> D25, 1A -> D26, 2A -> D27 (3,4EN, 3A, 4A to any other output pins, or 3,4EN to GND if unused).
- Pico: 1,2EN -> GP2, 1A -> GP3, 2A -> GP4.
- Raspberry Pi 4: 1,2EN -> GPIO18 (pin 12), 1A -> GPIO23 (pin 16), 2A -> GPIO24 (pin 18).
- Motor 1 between 1Y (pin 3) and 2Y (pin 6); motor 2 between 3Y (pin 11) and 4Y (pin 14).
- 100 nF ceramic capacitor from VCC1 to GND and from VCC2 to GND, close to the chip; add a bulk electrolytic (e.g. 100 uF) on VCC2.

## Using the driver
```python
from l293d import L293D
m1 = L293D(26, 27, en=25)    # 1A, 2A, 1,2EN on a PWM pin
m2 = L293D(14, 12)           # 3A, 4A with 3,4EN tied to 5 V (full speed)
m1.forward(); m2.reverse()
m1.forward(60)               # 60 % speed via PWM on the enable
m1.brake(); m1.coast()
```

## Gotchas
- VCC1 needs 5 V; on 3.3 V the chip is out of spec. The inputs still accept 3.3 V logic.
- No common ground = the motor twitches or does nothing.
- The bridge drops about 2.6-3.6 V: a 6 V motor on a 6 V supply runs slowly.
- 600 mA per channel is small: motor stall current often exceeds it, and the chip gets hot. The ground pins are the heat sink; on a PCB give them copper area.
- Motors on a USB 5 V pin can brown out the microcontroller. Use a separate battery on VCC2.
- The plain L293 (no D) has no clamp diodes: add external diodes if you got that one.
- Unused enable pins must not float: tie 3,4EN to GND if bridge 2 is unused.
